name: Color Picker
purpose: Edit, inspect, choose, and submit one color through a finished popup or inline editor with area, channel, format, preset, native chooser, and EyeDropper paths.
useWhen: A form, editor, or settings surface needs one color value with a finished visual editor.
Users need alpha, RGB, HSL, HSB, channel sliders, named presets, or a progressive platform color-picking path.

avoidWhen.condition: The interface only previews a color.
The task requires gradients, automatic color naming, contrast scoring, palette persistence, or a color wheel.
avoidWhen.useInstead: application-owned specialist behavior composed around Color Picker

composition: Place Label and Control inside Root; include HiddenInput when the value participates in native form submission.
For a popup, compose Trigger, Positioner, and Content. For an always-visible editor, set Root inline and render Content directly.
Build the visual editor from Area, ChannelSlider, format controls, channel inputs, and SwatchGroup; ValueSwatch and ValueText expose the current value.
Place SwatchIndicator inside Swatch or ValueSwatch whenever selection needs a visible non-color cue.

rules.statement: Use Brick parts for the finished interface and keep parsing, format conversion, selection, focus, dismissal, and form state in the exact Atom-backed machine.
Give the primary editable or native input an accessible name through Label or an explicit aria-label.
Provide name to Root and render exactly one HiddenInput when the color must submit.
Wrap popup Content in Positioner; do not recreate positioning, focus restoration, or outside dismissal.
Name every SwatchTrigger and render SwatchIndicator or an equivalent visible non-color selected cue.
Load styles.css, or core.css plus color-picker.css for modular delivery.
Treat NativeInput and EyeDropperTrigger as optional platform enhancements, not the only way to edit the color; unsupported EyeDropper triggers are disabled with data-unsupported.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reimplementing color conversion, pointer math, keyboard state, or popup behavior in Brick or application code.
commonMistakes.correction: Compose the released ColorPicker anatomy and controlled callbacks.

commonMistakes.mistake: Putting popup Content beside Root without Positioner.
commonMistakes.correction: Use Trigger, Positioner, and Content as the released popup composition.

commonMistakes.mistake: Naming both visible inputs and HiddenInput for submission.
commonMistakes.correction: Put name on Root and render one HiddenInput.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using raw color alone to show the selected preset.
commonMistakes.correction: Render SwatchIndicator and an accessible preset name.

validation: Test area and channel synchronization, alpha, RGB/HSL/HSB format changes, presets, text/native/EyeDropper paths, controlled state, popup focus and dismissal, disabled/read-only/invalid, form submit/reset, light/dark, forced colors, reduced motion, narrow/zoom, RTL, and non-color selection cues.
